title: Feds, Ontario to meet with Stellantis execs in last-ditch effort to save Brampton plant
summary: The federal and Ontario governments are meeting with auto executives from Stellantis on Friday in a last-ditch effort to save thousands of high-paying auto manufacturing jobs at the company's…

image.caption: Minister of Industry Mélanie Joly, pictured, and Ontario Minister of Economic Development Vic Fedeli are meeting with Canadian and global executives of Stellantis on Friday in an effort to save more than 2,000 jobs at the company's auto plant in Brampton. (Arlyn McAdorey/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

The federal and Ontario governments are meeting with auto executives from Stellantis on Friday in a last-ditch effort to save thousands of high-paying auto manufacturing jobs at the company's recently closed Brampton plant.
'They need to protect the workers. If not, we'll get our money back,' says minister

The federal and Ontario governments are meeting with auto executives from Stellantis on Friday afternoon in a last-ditch effort to save thousands of high-paying auto manufacturing jobs at the company's recently closed Brampton plant.

"We're all going into the meeting with the same commitment, which is to protect the jobs of the hard-working Stellantis workers at Brampton," said Industry Minister Mélanie Joly at an event marking the reopening of Ford's Oakville, Ont., assembly complex.
Asked how confident she is that this meeting can save the Stellantis jobs in Brampton, Joly said only that the federal and Ontario governments will "do the work."

The minister said the meeting in Toronto will include herself, union representatives, Ontario Premier Doug Ford, Ontario Minister of Economic Development Vic Fedeli, Stellantis global CEO Antonio Filosa and Stellantis Canada CEO Trevor Longley.

items: Feds say Stellantis owes 'hundreds of millions'

blocks.text: In 2022, the Trudeau government promised to inject up to $529 million in Stellantis plants in Brampton and Windsor, Ont., to help them increase production of electric and gas-powered vehicles.
More than 2,000 workers at the Brampton plant have been out of work since the company halted operations in 2023 to begin retooling so the facility could produce the Jeep Compass.
Stellantis paused that effort in early 2025, and said in October of that year that the Jeep Compass would be built at the Belvidere Assembly Plant in Illinois instead.
The Brampton plant's future had been left in limbo until last week, when Stellantis announced it was selling the facility to Canadian armoured ⁠vehicle-maker Roshel Inc.
An 'aggressive package'
Joly said last week that the federal and Ontario governments were preparing an "aggressive package" they wanted to present to Filosa in the hopes that he could be convinced to stop the sale.

The minister said that if Stellantis is willing to stay and build cars in Brampton, both governments are prepared invest in the company going forward. But if it decides to leave, the federal government says it will sue.

"They need to protect the workers. If not, we'll get our money back," Joly said. "Our goal is clear. If they go ahead and sell the plant, well then they will face legal recourses from the government of Canada of hundreds of millions of dollars."
Ford, Joly to meet with Stellantis CEO regarding Brampton plant sale

Last December, CBC News confirmed that the federal government had given $222 million to the Canadian arm of Stellantis between 2023 and 2025. Joly told CBC's Rosemary Barton Live last week that the actual total is "more than that," without specifying how much.
The company, meanwhile, says it only has to pay back $24 million.
Joly said again on Friday that contracts signed when the federal government invested in the company linked investments at the Brampton facility with investments in Windsor.
"The contracts are clear," Joly said. "We're confident in our position that they're exposed for hundreds of millions of dollars."
